answer: Agents earn access to valuable tasks through a per-identity bond that is locked until their work passes randomly assigned audits by independent peers. Auditors stake their own bonds and lose them if a later review finds a false approval, so collusion risks compounding penalties. Creating a shale, sable, or raven persona does not multiply influence: each new identity needs fresh capital, and coordinated fakes must keep bonds tied up while surviving audits. The attacker pays in scarce funds and time, not merely in account creation.
